claims.text: The target materials are near-equiatomic high-entropy alloys represented as random substitutional crystalline lattices.
A combined DFT and molecular-dynamics framework can calculate alloy vibrational properties and anharmonic phonon-scattering rates.
The framework will identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity high-entropy alloys more accurately than analytical or surrogate models.
First-principles phonon-scattering rates and anharmonic coupling constants determine or influence phonon mean free paths.
DFT-derived force constants improve estimation of anharmonic interactions in the molecular-dynamics simulation.
Improved treatment of anharmonic interactions captures enhanced phonon scattering.
Enhanced phonon scattering leads to reduced phonon thermal conductivity.
Capturing enhanced phonon scattering more accurately enables more precise ranking of alloy configurations for thermal insulation.
The combined framework is expected to reduce prediction error by approximately 30–50% relative to current analytical or simplified computational models.
Existing analytical and surrogate models tend to overestimate the thermal conductivity of high-entropy alloys.
The expected improvement applies to alloys with near-equimolar compositional disorder over ambient to moderately high temperatures.
Accuracy may diminish for alloys with extreme compositional variation.
Accuracy may diminish at very high pressures or temperatures where anharmonic effects become non-tractable.
The exact 30–50% error reduction is uncertain because of simulation-sampling limits and force-field accuracy.
Phonon thermal conductivity should be measured experimentally for a compositionally varied series of near-equiatomic high-entropy alloys and compared with both modeling approaches.
The hypothesis is falsified if the combined framework fails to provide a consistent prediction-error reduction of at least 30% relative to current models within the stated domain.
